text:
Alex: seeing a perf regression on canary after the batching heuristic tweak (rollout yesterday). 99th latency up ~40% on long seqs. linking the dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dash/abc123 :grimacing:

Sophia: ugh. I ran a quick nsys profile with nvtx+cuda. timeline shows a LOT more tiny kernels (10-30us) instead of the previous 2 larger kernels. looks like we’re spilling the batch into micro-batches.

Mike: can you paste the nvtx span view? my guess is we lost coalescing in the batcher switch. perfetto groups look fragmented when NVTX ranges are tiny.

Sophia: paste from nsys timeline (trimmed):
```
GPU Activity:
  0.000 ms - 0.250 ms : kernel_batch_forward (coalesced, 1024 tokens)
  0.251 ms - 0.280 ms : kernel_small_attention (1-8 tokens)
  0.281 ms - 0.310 ms : kernel_small_ffn (1-8 tokens)
  ... (many repeats x120)
```
Before change it was:
```
  0.000 ms - 5.200 ms : kernel_batch_forward (full batch)
```

Sophia: also saw increased cudaMemcpyAsync calls and frequent kernel launches -> higher launch overhead. nvtx markers from the batcher are generated per sub-batch now.

Jen: I bisected to a single commit: 4f2b9c3 — "introduce adaptive batch_split_threshold for latency smoothing". Reverting that commit locally restores the coalesced kernel timeline and brings p99 back.

Alex: nice find. so the heuristic shrank sub-batches too aggressively for long seq distributions. Did the commit change KV cache interactions? I worry about KV eviction churn causing extra warmups.

Jen: KV cache behavior unchanged in that commit. But when we split into many micro-batches, we hit more KV cache lookups per request and we end up rehydrating some KV pages more frequently -> extra memory ops. profiler shows ~2.3x increase in L2 cache miss stalls around KV access kernels.

Mike: interesting: I also saw an nvprof run where the occupancy of the main attention kernel dropped because the per-launch work size is smaller. fewer warps active per kernel -> less throughput.

Sophia: command I used for repro profiling:
```
nsys profile --output /tmp/canary_nvtx --trace=nvtx,cuda,cudnn --sample=none \ 
  --force-overwrite --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-start="batch_start" --capture-range-end="batch_end" \ 
  python -m rl_infer.benchmark --model rdx-small --seq 2048 --batch 16
```

Alex: perf-bot ran nightly traces and flagged this change at 03:12:22 UTC. deploy-bot shows rollout id rdo-2026-159: succeeded but canary latency alerted.

perf-bot: automated note: new regression fingerprint on profile/stacktrace grouping. See /profiles/2019003456/canary/*.nsys :robot_face:

Jen: plan: revert the adaptive threshold and add a guard to avoid splitting when seq_len_distribution.mean > 512 OR estimated_kernel_cost(seq) > X. Also add unit tests that assert NVTX coalescing for large batches.

Mike: agree. we should also add a perf test that runs nvtx capture in CI (nightly) and computes kernel-count delta vs baseline. if kernel_count increases > 30% fail.

Sophia: one more note — perfetto UI mis-synced NVTX labels on a few runs; added a short script to re-stamp NVTX ranges based on our tracer's monotonic ids. pushed as a follow-up: 8a7d2b1. doesn't fix the micro-batch problem but makes comparison easier.

Alex: thanks all. Jen, can you open a PR with the revert + guard? include the bisect notes and the nsys excerpts. assign to Mike for review. I'll schedule a canary rollback window if the PR looks safe. :thumbsup:

Jen: on it, PR #4723 inbound with smoke perf results. will ping when ready.

Mike: I'll run a comparative perfetto nvtx diff once PR is up.

Alex: ok, keep the channel posted. if anyone else hits similar noisy kernels, drop the nsys trace here.
